key_insight: Quantum circuit simulation cost is strongly family-dependent, so adding family-specific residual corrections to a shared predictor improves estimates of approximation threshold and runtime.
engineering_relevance: The model can replace time-consuming trial-and-error tuning for tensor-network simulators by predicting near-optimal settings from OpenQASM and execution context in about 50 ms.
method: Shared neural backbone for circuit-level cost prediction
Family-conditioned residual branches add algorithm-specific corrections
Uses pretrained family classifier plus heuristic gate-composition fingerprints
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 7–130 qubit circuits across 10 families, the method reached 79.5% exact threshold accuracy, 91.2% within one rung, and runtime prediction with R² = 0.82.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate family classification and representative training data; unseen circuit families or atypical entanglement patterns may reduce reliability.
paper_title: Family-Aware Residual Architecture for Predicting Quantum Circuit Simulation Performance
